note: Mastering English Library dictionary. Definitions, examples and Arabic by Mastering English Library. Levels: CEFR-J Wordlist (Tono Lab, TUFS) and Octanove Vocabulary Profile (CC BY-SA 4.0). IPA: ipa-dict (MIT).

senses.def: famous in stories and legends, and perhaps not real
ex: They searched for the fabled lost city.
The fabled treasure was never found.

senses.def: cloth used for making clothes, curtains and furniture
ex: The dress is made of soft fabric.
She chose a bright fabric for the curtains.

senses.def: the basic structure of a society or system
ex: Crime damages the fabric of society.

senses.def: to invent false information in order to trick people
ex: He fabricated evidence against his rival.
The report was fabricated.

senses.def: to make or build something, especially in a factory
ex: The parts are fabricated in Germany.

senses.def: a false statement or story that someone has invented
ex: The story was a complete fabrication.
He was caught in a fabrication.

senses.def: extremely good; wonderful
ex: We had a fabulous holiday.
You look fabulous in that dress.

senses.def: the front part of the head, with the eyes, nose and mouth
ex: She washed her face.
He had a smile on his face.

senses.def: a flat side or surface of something
ex: The north face of the mountain is very steep.

senses.def: to look or be positioned towards something
ex: My room faces the sea.
Please face the front.

senses.def: to deal with a difficult situation
ex: She faces many challenges.

mistake.wrong: I can't face with the problem.
mistake.note: face as a verb takes a direct object, with no preposition.

senses.def: relating to or on the face
ex: He has a serious facial expression.
The man had long facial hair.

senses.def: a beauty treatment for the skin of the face
ex: She booked a facial at the spa.

senses.def: to make an action or process possible or easier
ex: Technology can facilitate learning.
The new road will facilitate trade between the towns.
A good chair facilitates discussion in a meeting.

mistake.wrong: The app facilitates students to learn.
mistake.right: The app facilitates learning. / The app helps students (to) learn.
mistake.note: Do not use facilitate + person + to-infinitive. Its object is the process, not the person.

senses.def: buildings, equipment or services provided for a particular purpose
ex: The hotel has excellent sports facilities.
The school has poor facilities for disabled students.

senses.def: a place or building used for a particular activity
ex: The new sports facility opened last year.
It is a medical research facility.

senses.def: a useful feature of a machine or system
ex: The phone has a facility for recording calls.

senses.def: an exact copy of a document, picture or book
ex: The museum sells a facsimile of the old map.
This is a perfect facsimile.

senses.def: something that is known to be true or to have happened
ex: It is a fact that the Earth moves around the sun.
Tell me the facts.

senses.def: in fact: used to give more detail, or to say what is really true
ex: In fact, I have never been there.

senses.def: a small group within a larger group, with different aims or beliefs
ex: The party split into two factions.
Rival factions fought for power.

senses.def: one of several things that affect or cause a result
ex: Cost is an important factor in our decision.
Stress is a factor in many illnesses.

senses.def: a group of related subjects taught in a university, or the teachers in it
ex: She studies in the faculty of medicine.
The faculty of law has new courses.

senses.def: a natural ability, such as seeing or hearing
ex: Old people may lose their mental faculties.

senses.def: to slowly lose colour or brightness
ex: My jeans have faded in the sun.
The light faded as night came.

senses.def: to slowly become weaker and then disappear
ex: The sound faded away.
Hope began to fade.

senses.def: to not pass a test or exam
ex: He failed his driving test.
Many students fail the first time.

senses.def: to not succeed in doing something
ex: Their plan failed.
She failed to arrive on time.

senses.def: to stop working properly
ex: The brakes failed.

mistake.note: fail takes a direct object; do not add from or in.

senses.def: a lack of success, or something that does not succeed
ex: The plan ended in failure.
Her first business was a failure.

senses.def: a situation in which something stops working
ex: A power failure left the town in the dark.

senses.def: not strong or clear; hard to see, hear or smell
ex: I heard a faint noise.
There was a faint smell of smoke.

senses.def: feeling weak and as if you might fall
ex: I feel faint; I need to sit down.

senses.def: to suddenly become unconscious for a short time
ex: She fainted in the heat.
He nearly fainted at the sight of blood.

senses.def: a strong belief in the ability or goodness of someone or something
ex: I have great faith in my doctor.
She lost faith in the system.

senses.def: a strong belief in God, or a particular religion
ex: Faith gives him strength.
People of all faiths live here.

senses.def: staying loyal to a person, group or belief
ex: He was a faithful friend.
A dog is a faithful companion.

senses.def: accurate and close to the original
ex: The film is a faithful copy of the book.

senses.def: made to look real in order to trick people
ex: The police found fake money.
He wore a fake beard.

senses.def: to move down to the ground by accident or from a higher place
ex: Leaves fall in autumn.
She fell off her bike.

senses.def: to become lower in level or amount
ex: Prices fell last month.
The temperature fell below zero.

senses.def: to start to be in a particular state
ex: The baby fell asleep.
They fell in love.

senses.def: a drop to the ground; or a reduction in amount
ex: He broke his arm in a fall.
There was a sharp fall in sales.

mistake.note: fall is intransitive (no object); use drop when someone lets something fall.

senses.def: a false belief, or a mistake in reasoning
ex: It is a fallacy that money brings happiness.
The argument is based on a logical fallacy.

senses.def: having dropped to the ground
ex: Fallen leaves covered the path.
A fallen tree blocked the road.

senses.def: the state of being known by many people
ex: The singer rose to fame in 2010.
She did not want fame.

senses.def: known to you; easy to recognise
ex: Her face looks familiar.
It was a familiar song.

senses.def: knowing something well (followed by with)
ex: Are you familiar with this program?

mistake.wrong: I am familiar to this program.
mistake.right: I am familiar with this program.
mistake.note: Use familiar with for what you know; familiar to means 'known to' someone.

senses.def: a group of people related to each other, such as parents and children
ex: I have a big family.
My family lives in Cairo.

senses.def: a person with extreme and sometimes dangerous opinions
ex: A group of fanatics attacked the office.

senses.def: a person who is extremely keen on something
ex: He is a football fanatic.

senses.def: too enthusiastic or extreme in belief or interest
ex: He is fanatic about cleaning.

senses.def: special and expensive, not simple or plain
ex: They ate at a fancy restaurant.
I don't need anything fancy.

senses.def: a liking or wish for something
ex: She took a fancy to the red car.

senses.def: to want something or want to do something (British)
ex: Do you fancy a coffee?
I fancy going out tonight.

senses.def: extremely good; wonderful
ex: We had a fantastic holiday.
That's fantastic news!

senses.def: a pleasant situation you imagine but which is unlikely to happen
ex: He lives in a fantasy world.
Winning the lottery is just a fantasy.

senses.def: a type of story with magic and imaginary worlds
ex: She loves reading fantasy novels.

senses.def: at or to a long distance
ex: Is the station far from here?
We didn't walk far.

senses.def: by a great amount; much
ex: This is far better than the last one.

senses.def: the most distant of two things or places
ex: He lives on the far side of the river.

senses.def: a funny play with silly situations
ex: The theatre is showing a farce this week.

senses.def: a situation that is badly organised and ridiculous
ex: The meeting was a complete farce.

senses.def: an act of saying goodbye, especially for a long time
ex: They held a farewell party for her.
He waved a sad farewell.

senses.def: the work of growing crops or keeping animals on a farm
ex: Farming is hard work.
Many villagers live by farming.

senses.def: at or to a greater distance
ex: We walked farther than I expected.
The shop is farther down the street.

senses.def: extremely interested in something
ex: The children were fascinated by the magic show.
I'm fascinated by space.

senses.def: a very strong interest in something
ex: He has a fascination with old trains.
She watched with fascination.

senses.def: the style of clothes and appearance that is popular at a time
ex: She works in the fashion industry.
Short skirts are in fashion this year.

senses.def: a way of doing something
ex: He spoke in a calm fashion.

senses.def: moving or happening at high speed
ex: That is a fast car.
She is a fast runner.

senses.def: at high speed; quickly
ex: Don't drive so fast.
He talks very fast.

senses.def: causing death
ex: He was in a fatal car crash.
The disease is often fatal.

senses.def: causing very serious trouble or failure
ex: It was a fatal mistake to trust him.

senses.def: a death caused by an accident or violence
ex: There were no fatalities in the fire.
Road fatalities increased last year.

senses.def: the power that some believe controls events in your life
ex: Fate brought them together.
She believes in fate.

senses.def: what happens to someone, especially something bad
ex: No one knows the fate of the missing sailors.

senses.def: your male parent
ex: My father is a doctor.
Her father works in a bank.

senses.def: the father of your husband or wife
ex: My father-in-law lives next door.
She cooked dinner for her father-in-law.

senses.def: a feeling of being extremely tired
ex: Fatigue can cause accidents on the road.
She was ill with fatigue.

senses.def: responsibility for a mistake or bad situation
ex: It's my fault; I forgot.
Whose fault was the accident?

senses.def: a weakness in someone's character, or a problem in a machine
ex: Laziness is his biggest fault.
There is a fault in the engine.

mistake.note: Use fault, not guilt, for responsibility for a mistake; guilt is a feeling or a legal state.

senses.def: not working correctly because of a fault
ex: The shop replaced my faulty phone.
A faulty wire caused the fire.

senses.def: something kind you do to help someone
ex: Can you do me a favour?
He asked me for a favour.

senses.def: approval or support for someone or something
ex: Most people are in favour of the plan.

mistake.wrong: I made a favor to her.
mistake.note: We do a favour for someone; we do not 'make' it.

senses.def: a copy of a document sent through a phone line, or the machine that sends it
ex: I'll send you a fax this afternoon.
The office has a new fax.

senses.def: to send a document by fax
ex: Please fax the form to this number.
She faxed me the contract.

senses.def: the feeling you get when you are frightened or worried
ex: She has a fear of spiders.
He shook with fear.

senses.def: to be afraid of someone or something, or worried that something bad may happen
ex: Many people fear flying.
We fear the worst.

senses.def: very frightening in appearance or behaviour
ex: The dog looked fearsome.
He had a fearsome temper.

senses.def: a large, special meal for many people
ex: The family prepared a feast for the festival.
We had a wedding feast.

senses.def: an action that shows great skill, strength or courage
ex: Climbing the mountain in a day was an amazing feat.
It was a feat of engineering.

senses.def: relating to a system where states join under one central government
ex: The federal government controls defence.
The country has a federal system.

senses.def: comments about how good or useful something is, to help improve it
ex: The teacher gave me feedback on my essay.
We welcome your feedback.

mistake.right: I got a lot of feedback.
mistake.note: feedback is uncountable; do not add -s.

senses.def: to experience an emotion or physical state
ex: I feel happy today.
Do you feel cold?

senses.def: to touch something to find out what it is like
ex: Feel this soft cloth.
She felt his forehead.

senses.def: to have an opinion about something
ex: I feel that we should wait.

senses.def: the way something feels when you touch it
ex: I like the feel of this cloth.

senses.def: an emotion such as happiness or anger
ex: I had a strange feeling.
She has strong feelings about it.

senses.def: an opinion or belief that you are not completely sure about
ex: I have a feeling that he is lying.

senses.def: to pretend to have a feeling or condition
ex: He feigned illness to avoid work.
She feigned surprise.

senses.def: an old-fashioned word for a man
ex: He's a friendly fellow.

senses.def: sharing a situation or activity with you
ex: He helped his fellow students.
She thanked her fellow passengers.

senses.def: belonging to the sex that can have babies or lay eggs
ex: The female lion hunts for food.
She is the first female president.

senses.def: a female person or animal
ex: Females live longer than males in many species.

senses.def: extremely fierce, violent or strong
ex: A ferocious dog guarded the gate.
The storm was ferocious.

senses.def: extreme violence or force
ex: The tiger attacked with great ferocity.
The ferocity of the storm shocked us.

senses.def: a boat that carries people and vehicles across water
ex: We took the ferry to the island.
The ferry leaves every hour.

senses.def: to go to a place and bring back someone or something
ex: Please fetch my bag from the car.
I'll fetch the children from school.

senses.def: to be sold for a particular price
ex: The painting fetched a million pounds.

senses.def: an outdoor event with games and stalls, usually to raise money
ex: The village fete raised money for the school.

senses.def: a small number of; not many
ex: Few people came to the meeting.
I have a few friends here.

senses.def: a small number of people or things
ex: Many are invited, but few will come.
Only a few of us stayed.

mistake.note: Use few with countable nouns and little with uncountable nouns; a few means some, few means almost none.

senses.def: a substance in food that helps your body digest
ex: Beans are a good source of fibre.
Eat more fibre for a healthy gut.

senses.def: a thin thread used to make cloth or rope
ex: Cotton is a natural fibre.

senses.def: invented for a story and not real
ex: Sherlock Holmes is a fictional detective.
The film is set in a fictional country.

senses.def: to touch or move something with your fingers again and again
ex: Stop fiddling with your pen.

senses.def: to change figures or records dishonestly to get money
ex: He was fired for fiddling the accounts.

senses.def: a violin, especially when used to play folk music
ex: She plays the fiddle in a folk band.

senses.def: a person who plays the fiddle
ex: The fiddler played at the wedding.
A street fiddler stood by the station.

senses.def: a very cruel or evil person
ex: The writer described the killer as a fiend.

senses.def: a person who is very keen on something
ex: She is a fitness fiend.

senses.def: angry and ready to attack; frightening
ex: The dog had a fierce bark.
A fierce storm hit the coast.

senses.def: very strong or intense
ex: There is fierce competition for jobs.

senses.def: in a very strong, angry or determined way
ex: She fiercely defended her friend.
They fought fiercely for the title.

senses.def: one of five equal parts of something, or number 5 in order
ex: A fifth of the class was absent.
She finished in fifth place.

senses.def: an occasion when people hit each other, or an angry argument
ex: The two boys had a fight at school.
We had a fight about money.

senses.def: to use physical force against someone, or to take part in a war
ex: The soldiers fought bravely.
Two men were fighting in the street.

senses.def: to try hard to stop something bad
ex: Doctors are fighting the disease.

senses.def: violent action between people or armies
ex: Fighting broke out in the city.
The fighting lasted three days.

senses.def: in a way that uses words in a non-literal sense for effect
ex: She was figuratively walking on air.
Figuratively speaking, he is a lion.

senses.def: a number, especially one that is official
ex: Sales figures rose last year.
Write the figure in the box.

senses.def: the shape of a person's body
ex: She has a slim figure.

senses.def: an important person
ex: He is a famous political figure.

senses.def: to think or believe something after considering it
ex: I figure she is right.
I figured he would be late.

senses.def: to write all the necessary information on an official document
ex: Please fill in this form.
Fill in your name and address.

senses.def: a small amount of material put in a hole in a tooth
ex: The dentist gave me a filling.

senses.def: the food put inside a pie, cake or sandwich
ex: The pie has an apple filling.

senses.def: a story shown in moving pictures at the cinema or on TV
ex: We watched a funny film last night.
What's your favourite film?

senses.def: a roll of material used in a camera to take photographs
ex: I need a new roll of film.

senses.def: to record moving pictures with a camera
ex: They filmed the show in Rome.
She filmed the whole party.

senses.def: a device that lets liquid or air pass through while holding back dirt
ex: Change the water filter every month.
A coffee filter catches the grounds.

senses.def: coming at the end; last
ex: This is the final question.
The final bus leaves at ten.

senses.def: the last game in a competition
ex: Our team reached the final.
She won the final.

senses.def: after a long time or a lot of effort
ex: The bus finally arrived.
We finally found the key.

senses.def: used to introduce the last thing you want to say
ex: Finally, I would like to thank everyone.

senses.def: to provide the money for a project or business
ex: The government financed the new road.
She financed her studies with a part-time job.

senses.def: the management of money, especially by a company or country
ex: He works in finance.
She studied finance at university.

senses.def: relating to money
ex: The company has financial problems.
She gets financial help from her parents.

senses.def: in a way that relates to money
ex: He is financially independent.
The business is doing well financially.

senses.def: to see or get something you were looking for or did not expect
ex: I can't find my keys.
She found a wallet on the bus.

senses.def: to have an opinion about something after experiencing it
ex: I find this book very boring.
We found the hotel comfortable.

senses.def: to learn something by looking or asking
ex: Can you find out the time of the train?

senses.def: to get information about something because you want to know more about it
ex: Can you find out when the train leaves?
I found out that she had lied.

mistake.wrong: I want to know-out the price.
mistake.right: I want to find out the price.
mistake.note: Use find out for getting new information.

senses.def: information discovered through research or investigation
ex: The study's main findings were published today.
Police reported their findings to the court.

senses.def: well, healthy or happy
ex: "How are you?" "I'm fine, thanks."
The weather is fine today.

senses.def: good enough; acceptable
ex: Your answer is fine.
"Shall we meet at six?" "That's fine."

senses.def: very thin or made of very small pieces
ex: She has fine hair.

senses.def: an amount of money you must pay as a punishment
ex: He got a fine for parking here.
The fine is fifty pounds.

senses.def: in a satisfactory or good way
ex: The new system works fine.
Everything is going fine.

senses.def: to make someone pay money as a punishment
ex: The police fined him for speeding.
The company was fined £10,000.

senses.def: one of the long parts at the end of the hand
ex: She cut her finger on the knife.
He pointed his finger at the map.

senses.def: the heat and light from something burning
ex: Fire destroyed the old house.
We sat around the fire.

senses.def: to make someone leave their job
ex: The company fired him for being late.
She got fired last week.

senses.def: to shoot a gun or weapon
ex: The soldier fired his rifle.
Police fired at the car.

senses.def: a gun that a person can carry
ex: It is illegal to carry a firearm here.
Police found a firearm in the car.

senses.def: a space in a wall of a room where a fire can burn
ex: We sat by the fireplace in winter.
The fireplace keeps the room warm.

senses.def: a computer system that stops unauthorised access to a network
ex: The firewall blocked the virus.
Our company uses a strong firewall.

senses.def: fairly hard; not soft
ex: I prefer a firm mattress.
The ground was firm.

senses.def: showing strong and fixed beliefs
ex: She was firm with the children.

senses.def: a business or company
ex: He works for a law firm.
The firm has fifty employees.

senses.def: to become or make something harder or more solid
ex: Press the soil down to firm it.

senses.def: in a strong, steady or determined way
ex: He held the rope firmly.
I firmly believe it is wrong.

senses.def: coming before all others in time or order
ex: Today is my first day at work.
She came first in the race.

senses.def: before anything or anyone else
ex: First, wash your hands.
Who arrived first?

senses.def: used to introduce the first point in a list
ex: Firstly, we need more time.
Firstly, thank you for coming.

senses.def: healthy and strong, especially from exercise
ex: He plays football to stay fit.
She is fit for her age.

senses.def: good enough or suitable for a purpose
ex: The food was not fit to eat.

senses.def: to be the right size or shape for someone or something
ex: These shoes don't fit me.
The key fits the lock.

senses.def: to have enough space for something
ex: Will all the books fit in the box?

senses.def: the way clothes or things fit
ex: The jacket is a perfect fit.

senses.def: the number 5
ex: I have five brothers.
The shop opens at five.

senses.def: a way of solving a problem, often quick
ex: There is no quick fix for the problem.
The software update is a fix for the bug.

senses.def: to repair something that is broken
ex: Can you fix my bike?
He fixed the broken window.

senses.def: to decide or arrange a time or place
ex: Let's fix a date for the meeting.

senses.def: to fasten something firmly in place
ex: He fixed the shelf to the wall.

senses.def: not changing or able to be changed
ex: We pay a fixed price each month.
Meetings are held at a fixed time.

senses.def: firmly attached and not moving
ex: The table is fixed to the floor.

senses.def: a hot, bright piece of burning gas coming from a fire
ex: The candle flame moved in the wind.
The house burst into flames.

senses.def: to move up and down or from side to side quickly
ex: The bird flapped its wings.
The flag flapped in the wind.

senses.def: happening suddenly and lasting a very short time
ex: The town was hit by flash floods.

senses.def: a sudden bright light that lasts a short time
ex: There was a flash of lightning.
Don't use a flash in the museum.

senses.def: to shine brightly for a short time, or make a light do this
ex: The car flashed its lights.
Lightning flashed across the sky.

senses.def: a part of a film or book that shows a time in the past
ex: The film uses flashbacks to tell his past.
She had a flashback of the accident.

senses.def: a container for keeping drinks hot or cold, or a bottle used in a laboratory
ex: She brought a flask of hot tea.
The scientist filled the flask with water.

senses.def: to praise someone too much, often to please them
ex: He flattered his boss to get a promotion.
I was flattered by the invitation.

senses.def: praise that is not sincere, given to please someone
ex: Flattery will get you nowhere.
He used flattery to win her trust.

senses.def: the taste of food or drink
ex: The soup has a strong flavour.
Which ice-cream flavour do you want?

senses.def: a mistake or weakness that makes something not perfect
ex: There is a flaw in your argument.
The diamond had a small flaw.

senses.def: perfect, with no mistakes or faults
ex: Her English is flawless.
The singer gave a flawless performance.

senses.def: to leave a place quickly because you are in danger
ex: Thousands fled the war.
The thief fled from the scene.

senses.def: a group of ships or vehicles owned by one company or country
ex: The company has a fleet of delivery vans.
The navy sent a fleet to the coast.

senses.def: the soft part of the body of a person or animal, between skin and bone
ex: The knife cut into his flesh.
Many animals eat flesh.

senses.def: the soft inside part of a fruit or vegetable
ex: The flesh of the mango is sweet.

senses.def: able to change or be changed easily to suit a situation
ex: I have flexible working hours.
We need to be flexible about the plan.

senses.def: able to bend easily without breaking
ex: The toy is made of flexible plastic.

senses.def: to move something with a short, quick movement
ex: She flicked the switch.
He flicked the dust off his coat.

senses.def: a light that shines unsteadily
ex: The candle gave a weak flicker.
A flicker of light appeared in the window.

senses.def: a brief sign of a feeling
ex: There was a flicker of hope on her face.

senses.def: a journey in an aircraft
ex: Our flight was delayed.
I booked a flight to Dubai.

senses.def: the act of flying through the air
ex: A bird's flight is a beautiful sight.

senses.def: changing your mind or interests often and not being serious
ex: He is a flighty young man.
She was too flighty to stay in one job.

senses.def: to turn over quickly, or to make something do this
ex: Flip the pancake over.
The car flipped over in the crash.

senses.def: to press a switch to turn something on or off
ex: He flipped the light switch.

senses.def: to move quickly and lightly from one place to another
ex: Butterflies flitted among the flowers.
She flitted from room to room.

senses.def: a group of birds or sheep
ex: A flock of sheep crossed the road.
We saw a flock of birds.

senses.def: gates that control the flow of water in a river or canal
ex: They opened the floodgates to release water.

senses.def: open the floodgates: to allow a lot of something to start
ex: The decision opened the floodgates to complaints.

senses.def: to grow or develop well and be successful
ex: Small businesses flourish in the city.
Plants flourish in warm weather.

senses.def: a big movement made to attract attention
ex: He opened the door with a flourish.

senses.def: a smooth, continuous movement of liquid, air or electricity
ex: The flow of water was strong.
The dam controls the flow of the river.

senses.def: to move steadily and continuously, especially a liquid
ex: The river flows to the sea.
Traffic was flowing freely.

senses.def: an infectious illness like a very bad cold, with fever and aches
ex: I stayed home with the flu.
Half the class has flu.

mistake.note: Use the flu or just flu, not 'a flu'; it is usually uncountable.

senses.def: a change that happens often, especially in price or amount
ex: There are wide fluctuations in oil prices.
The fluctuation in temperature was large.

senses.def: likely to change; not fixed
ex: The situation is fluid.
We have fluid plans for the weekend.

senses.def: smooth and graceful
ex: The dancer made fluid movements.

senses.def: a musical instrument you blow into, held sideways
ex: She plays the flute in the school band.
He learned the flute at ten.

senses.def: to bend something so one part lies on another
ex: Fold the paper in half.
She folded the clothes neatly.

senses.def: a line where something has been folded
ex: Cut along the fold.

senses.def: people in general, or people of a particular type
ex: Some folk don't like cold weather.
The country folk are friendly.

senses.def: folk music: traditional music of a region
ex: He plays folk guitar.

senses.def: to go or come after someone or something
ex: Follow me, please.
A dog followed him home.

senses.def: to do what a rule, instruction or advice says
ex: Follow the instructions carefully.
Children should follow the rules.

senses.def: to understand an explanation or argument
ex: Sorry, I don't follow you.

mistake.note: follow takes a direct object with no preposition.

senses.def: a lack of good sense; a foolish act or idea
ex: It would be folly to ignore the warning.
Buying that old car was an act of folly.

senses.def: liking someone or something (followed by of)
ex: I am very fond of my aunt.
She is fond of chocolate.

senses.def: kind and affectionate, especially when remembering the past
ex: I have fond memories of my childhood.

mistake.note: fond is followed by of.

senses.def: things that people and animals eat
ex: I love Italian food.
Is there any food in the fridge?

mistake.right: I bought a lot of food.
mistake.note: In general, food is uncountable; foods is used only for different kinds of food.

senses.def: a person who does silly things or has little sense
ex: Don't be a fool; wear a coat.
I felt like a fool.

senses.def: to trick someone into believing something that is not true
ex: He fooled everyone with his story.
Don't let him fool you.

senses.def: showing a lack of good sense
ex: It was foolish to leave the door open.
What a foolish mistake!

senses.def: the part of the body at the end of the leg, that you stand on
ex: My foot hurts after the long walk.
He hurt his left foot.

senses.def: a unit of length equal to 30.48 centimetres
ex: The room is ten feet wide.

mistake.note: The plural of foot is feet, not foots.

senses.def: used to show who or what something is intended to help or be used by
ex: This gift is for you.
A knife is used for cutting.

senses.def: used to show how long something continues
ex: I have lived here for three years.
We waited for an hour.

senses.def: because (formal or literary)
ex: She was happy, for she had won.

mistake.wrong: I have lived here since three years.
mistake.right: I have lived here for three years.
mistake.note: Use for with a length of time and since with a starting point.

senses.def: not allowed by a rule or law
ex: Smoking is forbidden in this building.
The forest is forbidden to visitors.

senses.def: physical strength or power
ex: He pushed the door with great force.
The force of the wind broke the window.

senses.def: a group of people organised for a task, such as soldiers
ex: The police force is looking for him.

senses.def: to make someone do something they do not want to do
ex: Nobody forced you to go.
The rain forced us to stay inside.

mistake.wrong: They forced him to leave from the room.
mistake.right: They forced him to leave the room.
mistake.note: force someone to do something; the verb after it takes to.

senses.def: the part of the face between the eyes and the hair
ex: She wiped the sweat from her forehead.
He has a scar on his forehead.

senses.def: a person in charge of a group of workers
ex: The foreman told the workers to start.
He became foreman at the factory.

senses.def: the person who speaks for a jury
ex: The foreman read the jury's decision.

senses.def: using scientific methods to solve crimes
ex: Forensic experts examined the scene.
The forensic report proved he was guilty.

senses.def: a large area covered with trees
ex: We walked through the forest.
Forests are home to many animals.

senses.def: for all time; always
ex: I will love you forever.
Nothing lasts forever.

senses.def: for a very long time (informal)
ex: The bus took forever to come.

senses.def: to lose a right or something valuable because you broke a rule
ex: The team forfeited the game.
He forfeited his right to appeal.

senses.def: the loss of something as a penalty
ex: The law allows forfeiture of property.
Failure to pay results in forfeiture of the deposit.

senses.def: to not remember something
ex: I forgot her name.
Don't forget to call me.

senses.def: to stop thinking about something
ex: Forget it; it doesn't matter.

mistake.wrong: I forgot my keys at home.
mistake.right: I left my keys at home.
mistake.note: Use leave for putting something somewhere; forget means you did not remember it.

senses.def: to stop being angry with someone for something they did
ex: Please forgive me for being late.
She never forgave him for lying.

senses.def: looking sad, lonely and without hope
ex: The dog sat forlorn at the door.
She had a forlorn look on her face.

senses.def: serious and correct, used in official situations
ex: Please wear formal clothes to the interview.
He wrote a formal letter.

senses.def: something you must do as part of an official process
ex: Signing the form is just a formality.
There are some formalities to complete.

senses.def: correct and serious behaviour
ex: They greeted each other with formality.

senses.def: the process of forming something
ex: The formation of the club took months.
Cloud formation depends on temperature.

senses.def: a particular arrangement or pattern
ex: The planes flew in formation.

senses.def: happening or existing before, but not now
ex: He is a former teacher.
She met her former classmate.

senses.def: the first of two things you have just mentioned
ex: I prefer the former idea.

senses.def: at an earlier time
ex: The hotel was formerly a school.
Mr Brown, formerly of Leeds, is our new manager.

senses.def: causing fear or respect because of size, power or skill
ex: She is a formidable opponent.
The team faces a formidable challenge.

senses.def: a set of numbers or letters that express a rule in maths or science
ex: Use this formula to find the area.
H2O is the formula for water.

senses.def: a plan or method for achieving something
ex: There is no magic formula for success.

senses.def: forward, away from a place; used in fixed phrases
ex: They walked back and forth across the room.
From that day forth, he never lied.

senses.def: lucky; having good luck
ex: We were fortunate to have good weather.
She is fortunate to have such friends.

senses.def: a very large amount of money
ex: He made a fortune selling cars.
That bag costs a fortune.

senses.def: luck, especially what happens by chance
ex: Good fortune smiled on us.

senses.def: towards the front or the direction you are facing
ex: Please move forward.
She leaned forward to listen.

senses.def: the remains of an ancient animal or plant preserved in rock
ex: They found a fossil of a fish in the rock.
Scientists study fossils to learn about dinosaurs.

senses.def: dirty or very unpleasant, especially in smell or taste
ex: There was a foul smell in the room.
The water tasted foul.

senses.def: to start an organisation or institution
ex: She founded the company in 2005.
The school was founded in 1900.

mistake.note: found (start) has the past form founded; found is the past of find.

senses.def: the solid base on which a building or idea is built
ex: The builders laid the foundations of the house.
Good habits are the foundation of success.

senses.def: an organisation that provides money for charity or research
ex: The foundation gives money to schools.

senses.def: a structure that sends water up into the air
ex: Children played near the fountain.
There is a fountain in the square.

senses.def: the number 4
ex: I have four cousins.
The film starts at four.

senses.def: a wild animal like a small dog, with red-brown fur and a thick tail
ex: A fox ran across the field.
Foxes hunt at night.

senses.def: a number that is not whole, such as a half
ex: One half is a simple fraction.

senses.def: a very small part of something
ex: He finished the work in a fraction of the time.

senses.def: a pleasant smell, or a liquid you wear to smell nice
ex: The flowers have a sweet fragrance.
She bought a new fragrance.

senses.def: honest and direct in what you say, even if it is unwelcome
ex: Let me be frank with you.
She gave a frank answer.

senses.def: in an honest and direct way
ex: Frankly, I don't care.
She spoke frankly about her problems.

senses.def: the crime of cheating someone to get money
ex: He was arrested for tax fraud.
The company was accused of fraud.

senses.def: a person who pretends to be something they are not
ex: He turned out to be a fraud.

senses.def: to become very upset, scared or angry; freak out (informal)
ex: Mum will freak if she sees this mess.
He freaked out at the news.

senses.def: costing no money
ex: Entry to the museum is free.
I got a free ticket.

senses.def: not busy; having no plans
ex: Are you free on Friday?
I have some free time.

senses.def: able to do what you want; not controlled by anyone
ex: The prisoners were set free.

senses.def: without paying
ex: Children travel free on Sundays.
He got in free.

senses.def: to let someone leave a place where they were kept
ex: The police freed the hostages.
They freed the bird from the net.

mistake.wrong: The ticket is free of cost.
mistake.note: free already means 'costing nothing', so 'free of cost' is unnecessary.

senses.def: the right to do what you want without being controlled
ex: People fought for their freedom.
Freedom of speech is important.

senses.def: without being controlled or limited
ex: People can speak freely here.
Birds fly freely in the garden.

senses.def: to become hard and solid because of cold, or to make something do this
ex: Water freezes at zero degrees.
You can freeze the leftover soup.

senses.def: to stop moving suddenly, for example from fear
ex: She froze when she heard a noise.

senses.def: a machine that keeps food very cold so it stays frozen
ex: Put the ice cream in the freezer.
We keep fish in the freezer.

senses.def: extremely cold
ex: It's freezing outside.
I'm freezing; close the window.

senses.def: how often something happens
ex: The frequency of buses has increased.
Accidents are happening with greater frequency.

senses.def: the number of waves per second, for example in radio
ex: The radio station uses a high frequency.

senses.def: happening or done often
ex: He makes frequent trips to London.
Frequent hand washing stops germs spreading.

senses.def: often; many times
ex: She frequently visits her grandmother.
This mistake occurs frequently.

senses.def: newly made or picked; not old or from a tin
ex: I bought fresh bread.
We ate fresh fruit.

senses.def: clean, cool and pleasant
ex: Open the window to get fresh air.

senses.def: new and different from before
ex: She wants a fresh start.

senses.def: a student in the first year of university or high school (US)
ex: She is a freshman at college.
The freshmen met in the main hall.

senses.def: a person you know well and like
ex: She is my best friend.
I'm meeting a friend for lunch.

mistake.right: He is a friend of mine.
mistake.note: Use a friend of mine, or he is friends with me; the noun needs an article or plural.

senses.def: behaving in a kind, pleasant way towards others
ex: The staff were very friendly.
He has a friendly smile.

senses.def: a relationship between friends
ex: Our friendship has lasted twenty years.
She values his friendship.

senses.def: a sudden feeling of fear
ex: The loud noise gave me a fright.
She screamed in fright.

senses.def: feeling afraid or worried
ex: The child was frightened of the dark.
I was frightened that I'd fail.

senses.def: to play and move about in a happy, lively way
ex: Lambs frolicked in the field.
Children frolicked in the sea.

senses.def: used to show the place or time where something starts
ex: I walk from home to school.
The shop is open from nine to five.

senses.def: used to show where a person or thing comes from
ex: She is from Egypt.
This cheese comes from France.

senses.def: used to show what something is made of
ex: Wine is made from grapes.

mistake.note: Do not use the before most country names after from.

senses.def: at or near the front of something
ex: Please use the front door.
I sat in the front row.

senses.def: the part of something that faces forward
ex: The garden is at the front of the house.
In front of me was a river.

senses.def: a line that separates two countries
ex: They crossed the frontier at night.
The frontier is closed.

senses.def: the furthest limit of knowledge or activity
ex: Scientists are exploring the frontiers of space.

senses.def: a thin white layer of ice on surfaces when it is very cold
ex: There was frost on the grass this morning.
The first frost came in November.

senses.def: to cover something with a thin layer of ice
ex: The cold frosted the windows.

senses.def: very cold, with frost
ex: It was a frosty morning.
Her breath showed in the frosty air.

senses.def: unfriendly and cold in manner
ex: He gave me a frosty look.

senses.def: turned to ice; very cold, or stored at very low temperature
ex: The lake is frozen.
I bought frozen peas.

senses.def: unable to move because of fear
ex: She stood frozen with fear.

senses.def: the point at which a plan or idea produces results
ex: After years of work, the plan came to fruition.
His dream finally reached fruition.

senses.def: feeling upset or angry because you cannot do or change something
ex: I was frustrated by the slow internet.
She felt frustrated at work.

senses.def: the feeling of being upset because you cannot do something
ex: He shouted in frustration.
The delays caused a lot of frustration.

senses.def: a substance such as petrol or coal that is burned to produce heat or power
ex: The car is running out of fuel.
Wood is used as fuel.

senses.def: to do or achieve what was hoped for or promised
ex: She fulfilled her dream of becoming a doctor.
The company fulfilled its promise.

senses.def: to meet a requirement or need
ex: He fulfils all the requirements for the job.

senses.def: containing as much as possible; having no empty space
ex: The bus is full.
My glass is full of water.

senses.def: having eaten enough food
ex: No more, thanks; I'm full.

senses.def: complete; including everything
ex: Please write your full name.

mistake.wrong: The glass is full with water.
mistake.right: The glass is full of water.
mistake.note: full is followed by of, not with.

senses.def: working or studying for the whole normal working week
ex: She has a full-time job.
He is a full-time student.

senses.def: for the whole normal working week
ex: She works full-time.
He studies full-time.

senses.def: completely; in every way
ex: I am fully aware of the risks.
The hotel is fully booked.

senses.def: enjoyment; a good time
ex: We had a lot of fun at the party.
Learning to swim is fun.

senses.def: enjoyable and entertaining
ex: It was a fun trip.
She's a fun person to be with.

mistake.wrong: We had a funny time at the party.
mistake.right: We had fun at the party.
mistake.note: funny means 'making you laugh'; for enjoyment say fun or a fun time.

senses.def: designed to be useful rather than attractive
ex: The kitchen is simple and functional.
He prefers functional furniture.

senses.def: able to work properly
ex: The machine is fully functional now.

senses.def: an amount of money saved or collected for a purpose
ex: They started a fund for the school.
The charity raised funds for flood victims.

senses.def: to provide money for something
ex: The government funds the new hospital.
The trip was funded by a local company.

senses.def: forming the basic and most important part of something
ex: Honesty is fundamental to friendship.
There is a fundamental difference between the two plans.

senses.def: a ceremony held when a dead person is buried or burned
ex: Many people went to his funeral.
The funeral will be held on Friday.

senses.def: a style of dance music with a strong rhythm
ex: She loves to dance to funk.
The band plays funk and soul.

senses.def: modern and interesting in an unusual way
ex: She wore a funky hat.
It's a funky little café.

senses.def: having a strong dance rhythm
ex: The band played a funky tune.

senses.def: making you laugh
ex: That joke is really funny.
He is a funny person.

senses.def: strange or unusual
ex: There's a funny smell in here.

senses.def: the thick soft hair that covers some animals
ex: The cat has soft grey fur.
The rabbit's fur is white.

senses.def: extremely angry
ex: She was furious with her brother.
He was furious about the delay.

senses.def: additional; more
ex: Do you need any further information?
Wait for further instructions.

senses.def: at or to a greater distance, or to a greater degree
ex: We can't go any further.
Let's discuss this further tomorrow.

senses.def: used to add another point to what you have said
senses.ar: علاوة على ذلك؛ فضلاً عن ذلك
ex: The room is small; furthermore, it is dark.
Furthermore, the price is very low.

senses.def: to join together to form one thing
ex: The two companies fused into one.
The bones fused after the break.

senses.def: to stop working because a fuse has melted
ex: The lights fused during the storm.

senses.def: the joining of different things into one
ex: The restaurant serves a fusion of Asian and French food.
The band plays a fusion of jazz and rock.

senses.def: the joining of atoms to produce energy
ex: The sun's energy comes from nuclear fusion.

senses.def: unnecessary worry or excitement about something unimportant
ex: Don't make a fuss about it.
What a fuss over nothing!
